newsitem.title: CONGO: Mandela to call new Zaire talks, Mobutu quit offer.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to call new Zaire talks, Mobutu quit offer.

text.p: South Africa's Nelson Mandela will call a fresh round of talks between Zaire's civil war foes in up to 10 days, a communique issued after a first meeting on Sunday said.

Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko had offered to hand over to an elected president but rebel leader Laurent Kabila was insisting that the rebels be made the transitional authority, mediators at the shipborne summit said.
Mandela told a news conference on the SAS Outeniqua that the fresh round of talks would be to "narrow the gap between the two parties".
He said Kabila had issued orders to his forces to stop advancing ahead of the talks but that this did not constitute a ceasefire.
"The question of a ceasefire is not part of his (Kabila's) vocabulary. What he is concerned with is that negotiations will lead to the end of hostilities," Mandela said.

U.N. and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said in initial remarks that Mobutu had offered to hand power to an elected president with a transitional authority organising elections.
